Configure Session Credentials for a Philips Hue Bridge

Source: R/client.R
hue_auth.Rd

Stores, retrieves, or clears default Philips Hue Bridge connection settings in an internal session environment so individual API calls do not need to pass a bridge object repeatedly.

Usage

hue_auth(
  ip = NULL,
  app_key = NULL,
  verify_ssl = NULL,
  ca_cert = NULL,
  clear = FALSE
)

Arguments

ip

Character scalar. IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname of the local Philips Hue Bridge (e.g., "192.168.1.50"). If NULL, falls back to session state set by hue_auth() and then the HUE_BRIDGE_IP environment variable.

app_key

Character scalar. Application key (hue-application-key) obtained via hue_create_app_key(). If NULL, falls back to session state set by hue_auth() and then the HUE_APP_KEY environment variable.

verify_ssl

Logical scalar. Whether to verify the bridge TLS certificate. Defaults to TRUE. Because local Philips Hue Bridges present a self-signed certificate signed by the Hue Bridge Root CA, either supply ca_cert with the path to the Signify Root CA PEM file or explicitly set verify_ssl = FALSE on trusted local networks.

ca_cert

Optional character scalar path to a PEM CA certificate bundle (such as the Philips Hue Bridge Root CA) used for TLS verification.

clear

Logical scalar. If TRUE, clears all stored session settings.

Value

Invisibly returns a hue_bridge object when ip and app_key are available, or NULL when cleared or unconfigured.

See also

hue_bridge(), hue_create_app_key()

Examples

hue_auth(ip = "192.168.1.50", app_key = "demo-key", verify_ssl = FALSE)
hue_auth()
hue_auth(clear = TRUE)
